stories.headline: Trump Says He Would 'Rather Not Have' USMCA as Trade Deal Renewal Deadline Approaches
stories.summary:
President Trump on Wednesday said he would "rather not have" the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the free-trade pact he signed during his first term, raising the prospect that the deal could collapse ahead of its July 1 renewal deadline. Trump made the remarks to reporters in Paris on the sidelines of the G7 summit, saying he was unsure whether a new deal could be reached.

The USMCA has underpinned North American trade since replacing NAFTA and is especially critical for Canada, which sends roughly 75 percent of its exports to the United States. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney left the G7 summit without a formal bilateral meeting with Trump, though Carney downplayed any suggestion of a diplomatic snub, saying he had held seven or eight discussions with the president over 36 hours covering trade, Ukraine, Iran, and other issues.

Canadian trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said talks with U.S. Trade Ambassador Jamieson Greer at the summit produced progress, though uncertainty about the deal's future remains elevated. LeBlanc has previously suggested Washington might seek annual review provisions that would introduce ongoing uncertainty about the pact's permanence.

Supporters of the agreement argue it integrates three tightly linked economies and that its collapse would raise costs for consumers and businesses across all three countries. Critics of the current terms, including some in the Trump administration, contend the deal contains imbalances that disadvantage American workers and manufacturers.

stories.headline: RFK Jr. Announces $700 Million Federal Investment in Addiction and Behavioral Health Services
stories.summary:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced Wednesday a federal investment of more than $700 million in behavioral health programs aimed at combating addiction and mental illness, which administration officials linked to homelessness. The announcement included a $96 million funding opportunity for the Trump administration's STREETS program — an acronym for Safety Through Recovery, Engagement, and Evidence-based Treatment and Support.

Kennedy, who has publicly described his own recovery from heroin addiction, made the announcement at an Easterseals behavioral health clinic in Clinton Township, Michigan. He indicated a particular emphasis on directing funding toward faith-based recovery organizations, a priority that reflects the administration's broader approach to social services.

Supporters of the initiative argue that faith-based organizations have a strong track record in addiction recovery and are often embedded in communities in ways that government agencies are not. Critics of faith-based funding models have raised concerns about the separation of church and state and whether secular recovery options remain adequately funded for those who prefer them.

The announcement comes as the administration has signaled a broader effort to reorient federal health and social spending under Kennedy's leadership at HHS.

stories.headline: Update: Trump Blocks Jay Clayton's DNI Confirmation Hearing, Linking Intelligence Post to Voting Bill
stories.summary:
President Trump abruptly directed his director of national intelligence nominee, Jay Clayton, not to appear before the Senate Intelligence Committee on Wednesday, effectively scuttling a confirmation hearing that Republican leaders had been trying to fast-track. Trump announced the delay in an early-morning Truth Social post, tying Clayton's confirmation process to Congress passing his voting legislation — a bill that has already failed once in the Senate.

Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Tom Cotton, who had initially vowed to proceed with the hearing regardless, was forced to announce its postponement after Trump's directive. The move also extended the lapse of powerful U.S. surveillance tools that require Senate-confirmed leadership to fully authorize. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer accused Trump of 'holding our national security hostage' for legislative leverage.

Clayton's nomination had been seen as a way to ease tensions between the White House and Senate Republicans after Trump installed Bill Pulte as acting intelligence chief. Republicans have expressed frustration that the White House is conditioning a national security appointment on unrelated legislative demands. Democrats on the Senate Intelligence Committee scheduled a press conference to condemn the delay.

The standoff highlights a recurring tension in Trump's second term between the executive branch's desire to use confirmations as legislative leverage and the Senate's constitutional role in advising and consenting on nominations. Critics from both parties warned the move leaves a critical intelligence post in limbo at a sensitive moment in U.S. foreign policy.

stories.headline: Update: Iranian Oil Tankers Cross U.S. Blockade Line in Gulf of Oman Ahead of Friday Deal Signing
stories.summary:
Three Iranian crude oil tankers owned by the sanctioned National Iranian Tanker Company — Diona, Hero II, and Sonia I — passed the U.S. naval blockade line in the Gulf of Oman on Wednesday, ship-tracking data shows. The move marks the first time these vessels have broadcast their locations since March and would represent Iran's first oil exports in two months if they reach their destinations.

Despite President Trump announcing Sunday the 'immediate removal' of the blockade following the U.S.-Iran framework agreement, U.S. naval forces have confirmed the blockade remains in effect until a formal deal is signed in Switzerland on Friday. Maritime analyst Michelle Wiese Bockman told BBC Verify the tankers' movement signals that 'Iran is confident the blockade is over, even if the U.S. has insisted it will be in place until Friday.'

The three ships are carrying a combined 3.8 million barrels of crude oil, according to TankerTrackers.com. They are not broadcasting planned destinations. The U.S. blockade had cut Iran's crude exports to roughly 260,000 barrels per day in May — less than a fifth of the 2025 average — the lowest level in six years.

The development adds tension to the final days before Friday's anticipated signing ceremony, with Iran-linked vessels becoming 'noticeably more active globally' since the deal announcement, according to monitoring group United Against Nuclear Iran. The episode illustrates the gap between Trump's public declaration that the blockade was lifted and the operational reality on the water, raising questions about enforcement and the durability of pre-signing commitments.

stories.headline: FTC and Four States Sue Leading Transgender Health Organization Over Pediatric Care Claims
stories.summary:
The Federal Trade Commission and four states filed suit Wednesday against the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH), the leading medical organization focused on transgender health, alleging it made false and unsubstantiated claims to parents in order to sell pediatric medical transition services. The lawsuit represents the Trump administration's most direct legal action yet against an institution involved in gender-affirming care for minors.

The FTC's complaint alleges WPATH deceived parents about the medical necessity and safety of medical transition procedures for children. WPATH's guidelines are widely cited by clinicians and insurers in determining standards of care for transgender youth, giving the case potential ripple effects across the broader healthcare system.

Supporters of the action argue that parents deserve accurate information about the evidentiary basis for pediatric transition treatments, pointing to recent reviews in several European countries that have restricted such care pending further research. Opponents contend the lawsuit is politically motivated, that WPATH's standards reflect mainstream medical consensus, and that the action will chill legitimate healthcare for vulnerable minors.

The lawsuit is the latest in a series of Trump administration moves against gender-affirming care, following executive orders and agency guidance restricting such treatments. Legal experts expect the case to face significant scrutiny over whether the FTC has jurisdiction over a medical professional association's clinical guidelines.

stories.headline: SpaceX-Tesla Mega-Merger Discussed as Possible Next Move for Elon Musk
stories.summary:
Reports surfaced Wednesday that Elon Musk is exploring a potential merger of SpaceX and Tesla, two of his most valuable companies, in what would be one of the largest corporate combinations in history. Legal experts cited in coverage said minority shareholders would have limited ability to block such a deal given Musk's dominant voting control over both entities.

SpaceX completed a record-breaking IPO earlier this month and subsequently acquired AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion. A merger with Tesla would create an entity spanning electric vehicles, energy storage, satellite internet, rocket launch services, and artificial intelligence — a conglomerate with few historical precedents in scope.

The prospect raises significant governance and regulatory questions. Tesla's public shareholders would likely face dilution concerns and conflicts of interest given Musk's control of both companies, while antitrust regulators would need to assess whether combining the firms' overlapping AI, energy, and transportation businesses creates anticompetitive conditions.

Musk has not publicly confirmed merger discussions. The report follows a period of intense activity across his business empire and comes as Tesla faces competitive pressure in the global EV market. Analysts said the move, if pursued, would test the limits of founder-controlled corporate governance.

stories.headline: UK Prime Minister Starmer Faces Cabinet Pressure to Step Down Days After By-Election Loss
stories.summary:
Senior members of British Prime Minister Keir Starmer's cabinet are expected to tell him in the coming days to agree to a transfer of power, according to Bloomberg Politics, following a significant by-election defeat. Supporters of Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham are among those anticipating the push, with the expectation that coordinated pressure from within Starmer's own government could make his position untenable.

The development represents a serious internal crisis for the Labour government, which came to power in 2024 after a landslide election victory. A loss in a key by-election has apparently accelerated dissatisfaction among senior party figures and cabinet members who had previously contained their concerns publicly.

Burnham, a prominent Labour figure with a national profile built during his tenure overseeing Greater Manchester, is widely seen as a potential successor. The situation echoes past British political crises in which governing party leaders faced coordinated internal pressure to vacate office rather than endure a formal leadership challenge vote.

stories.headline: Gilgo Beach Serial Killer Rex Heuermann Sentenced to Multiple Life Terms for Murdering Eight Women
stories.summary:
Rex Heuermann, the architect known as the Gilgo Beach serial killer, was sentenced Wednesday to multiple consecutive life terms in prison after admitting to the murders of eight women whose remains were found scattered along remote Long Island beaches. Judge Timothy Mazzei handed down the maximum sentence — three life terms for first-degree murder plus 25 years to life on four second-degree murder charges, all running consecutively — in a Riverhead, New York courtroom that erupted in cheers.

The victims, killed between 1993 and 2010, included women ranging in age from 20 to 34. Heuermann, 62, gave a brief statement before sentencing acknowledging responsibility but admitting his words carried "no meaning." Victims' family members delivered raw and emotional statements; the sister of one victim, who said she was 15 when Heuermann called their family after killing her sister, told him directly: "Save me a spot in hell because I'll see you there."

Heuermann, a married father of two from the Long Island suburb of Massapequa Park, was arrested in 2023 after the case went unsolved for more than a decade. He had initially pleaded not guilty before ultimately confessing. Suffolk County District Attorney Ray Tierney, addressing the families after the sentence, said: "I want them to get their revenge by going on to have wonderful lives — now it's time for them to heal."

stories.headline: UN Secretary-General Guterres Visits Haiti as Gang Violence Displaces 1.5 Million
stories.summary:
United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres traveled to Port-au-Prince on Tuesday for a one-day visit as newly released UN statistics revealed the depth of Haiti's crisis: 2,300 people killed and 100 kidnapped so far in 2026, with 1.5 million Haitians displaced from their homes. More than 300,000 people in Port-au-Prince alone have been driven out by gang violence, a record figure, with the powerful Viv Ansanm gang federation — designated a foreign terrorist organization by the United States — estimated to control 70 percent of the capital.

Guterres's first stop was the headquarters of a new gang-suppression force approved by the UN Security Council in September, which replaces an underfunded Kenyan police-led mission. Jamaica, Chad, El Salvador, and Guatemala have so far deployed fewer than 1,000 troops combined; the force is expected to begin operations in the coming weeks alongside Haiti's national police and growing armed forces.

The visit came shortly after more than 30 people were killed, injured, or reported missing in a single weekend in the Cité Soleil slum. Guterres also met privately with Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, who faces mounting international pressure to organize elections in a country of nearly 12 million people that has had no functioning elected government. The IOM's Haiti chief described the displacement situation as "entering an even more alarming phase."

stories.headline: Update: G7 Issues Joint Declaration Backing Ukraine, Threatening Fresh Russia Sanctions
stories.summary:
G7 leaders, including President Trump, signed a joint declaration Wednesday pledging unwavering support for Ukraine and committing to strengthen sanctions against Russia, including on its oil and gas sectors. The declaration marks a significant convergence between Trump and European allies, who had been at odds over Ukraine policy for much of his second term. The statement credits the U.S.-Iran agreement with creating new space to increase economic pressure on Moscow.

The declaration commits leaders to increase delivery of air defense systems, interceptors, and long-range capabilities to Ukraine, and to consider licensing arrangements to boost Ukrainian domestic military production. Zelenskyy, who joined the G7 session, said all seven nations unanimously support Ukraine and that Patriot missile supply and production expansion were discussed. The talks lasted only 75 minutes.

Trump separately told reporters that sanctions on Russian oil, partially suspended in March to ease prices during the Iran conflict, can now be reimposed as the Strait of Hormuz reopens. 'Soon we'll be able to do that because the oil is now flowing,' Trump said. The UK simultaneously announced new sanctions targeting Russia's shadow oil fleet and financial networks used to evade Western restrictions.

The joint declaration represents a notable shift in U.S. posture under Trump, who had previously been skeptical of deep involvement in the Ukraine conflict. European leaders, now the primary providers of military and financial aid to Kyiv, welcomed the alignment. Russia had conducted a major drone and missile barrage on Ukrainian cities hours before the summit opened Monday, killing 11 people.

stories.headline: Federal Reserve Issues First Rate Decision Under New Chairman Kevin Warsh
stories.summary:
The Federal Reserve on Wednesday handed down its first interest rate decision under newly installed Chairman Kevin Warsh, a closely watched moment for markets and consumers as inflation continues to rise. Futures markets overwhelmingly anticipated the Fed would hold rates steady, though the announcement marks the beginning of a new era of leadership at the central bank following Warsh's confirmation.

Warsh, a former Fed governor and Wall Street veteran nominated by President Trump, takes the helm at a sensitive juncture. Persistent inflation has complicated the case for rate cuts, while higher borrowing costs continue to weigh on housing affordability, consumer credit, and business investment for millions of Americans.

The decision carries broad implications for mortgage rates, auto loans, credit card interest, and savings yields. Any shift in tone or forward guidance from Warsh in his first press conference as chair will be scrutinized for signals about the Fed's path through the remainder of 2026.

stories.headline: Update: Armed Men Abduct Six-Year-Old Ebola Patient from DR Congo Hospital
stories.summary:
Armed men stormed a hospital in Butembo, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, and forcibly removed a six-year-old Ebola patient and her mother, local health official Dr. Lubambo Maboko Gaston said. The child was taken from Wanamahika Hospital by men described as 'very angry' and carrying knives. Authorities are now searching for the pair, with health officials warning that the child and mother risk worsening their condition and infecting others.

The incident is the latest in a series of attacks on Ebola treatment facilities during the current outbreak, which has now claimed nearly 200 lives and recorded approximately 840 confirmed cases. Last month police fired warning shots to disperse crowds attempting to reclaim bodies from a health facility, and isolation tents were set ablaze at another hospital. Misinformation has fueled widespread hostility toward treatment centers, with some residents believing Ebola is fabricated by outside organizations.

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no approved vaccine currently exists. The WHO has warned that active conflict in eastern Congo, where the M23 rebel group controls large portions of the affected provinces, is severely hampering containment efforts. Officials say it could be months before a vaccine candidate is ready.

stories.headline: Update: Trump Suffers Rare Endorsement Loss as Georgia Governor's Race Goes to Rick Jackson; Moore Wins Alabama Senate Runoff
stories.summary:
Georgia Republicans dealt a significant blow to President Trump on Tuesday, with healthcare executive and billionaire Rick Jackson defeating Trump-backed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in the Republican gubernatorial runoff. The loss marks the second time a Trump endorsee has fallen in a major statewide Georgia race this cycle, underscoring the limits of presidential influence in the state even within the GOP.

In brighter news for Trump, Rep. Barry Moore won the Alabama Republican Senate runoff, defeating former Navy SEAL Jared Hudson 58.7% to 41.3%, securing the nomination for the seat being vacated by Tommy Tuberville. In Oklahoma, Rep. Kevin Hern won the Senate primary, while the governor's race is heading to a runoff between Attorney General Gentner Drummond and Trump-backed Mike Mazzei.

In Georgia's Senate race, Trump-endorsed Rep. Mike Collins defeated former football coach Derek Dooley and will now face Democratic incumbent Sen. Jon Ossoff in November — a race Republicans view as critical to maintaining Senate control. Ossoff is well-funded and has previously won statewide in Georgia, making the contest one of the most competitive of the cycle.

The results present a mixed picture for Trump's political standing heading into the November midterms. Supporters note his endorsed candidate Collins is positioned well for the Senate fight and Moore's Alabama win was decisive, while critics point to the Georgia governor's loss as evidence that Trump's endorsement alone cannot guarantee victory in competitive Republican primaries.

stories.headline: Trump Administration Moves Civil Rights and Special Education Oversight Out of Department of Education
stories.summary:
The Trump administration announced Tuesday it is transferring two major functions from the Department of Education as part of its broader effort to dismantle the agency. The Justice Department will assume responsibility for civil rights enforcement in education, while the Department of Health and Human Services will take over oversight of special education programs.

Secretary of Education Linda McMahon said the changes better align the needs of specific student populations with the agencies most relevant to their circumstances. The administration has framed the restructuring as improving efficiency and ensuring more targeted federal support.

Critics, including disability rights advocates and civil liberties groups, warned the moves will undermine protections for minority students, students with disabilities, and other vulnerable populations. Opponents argue that consolidating these functions under agencies with broader mandates risks diluting the focused oversight that a dedicated education department provides.

The announcement is the latest step in the administration's stated goal of significantly shrinking or eliminating the Department of Education, a long-standing priority of conservatives who argue federal involvement in education should be reduced and decision-making returned to states and localities.

stories.headline: Modi Warns of 'Trust Deficit' as He Meets Trump on Sidelines of G7 Summit
stories.summary:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with President Donald Trump at the G7 summit in France on Wednesday, their first bilateral meeting in over a year. Despite an outwardly cordial exchange of handshakes and mutual praise, Modi signaled concern about a growing trust deficit between the two nations, reflecting a series of setbacks in U.S.-India relations since their last meeting.

The relationship has faced friction over a range of issues including trade disputes, tariffs, and geopolitical alignment, particularly as the Trump administration has pursued a more transactional foreign policy posture. India has sought to balance its ties with the United States against its longstanding relationships with Russia and other powers.

The G7 meeting in France has been overshadowed by broader tensions involving Trump's tariff threats and the geopolitical fallout from the U.S.-Iran interim deal. Modi's public acknowledgment of a trust shortage is notable given the historically warm personal rapport the two leaders have cultivated and India's strategic importance as a counterweight to China in the Indo-Pacific.

stories.headline: Tropical System Along Gulf Coast Threatens Life-Threatening Flooding from Texas to Florida Panhandle
stories.summary:
A cluster of storms along the Gulf Coast has a 70% chance of becoming the first named tropical storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season, the National Hurricane Center warned Tuesday. The system was centered roughly 55 miles south-southwest of Corpus Christi, Texas, with maximum sustained winds near 30 mph — just below the 39 mph threshold for tropical storm designation.

National Hurricane Center Director Michael Brennan warned that the primary danger is severe flooding from heavy rainfall, with potentially life-threatening flash flooding forecast from the Texas coast eastward into central Mississippi through Thursday. Isolated rainfall totals could reach a foot in coastal areas, with tornadoes also possible across southern Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and the Florida Panhandle.

Houston, which is hosting a FIFA World Cup match between Portugal and the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Wednesday, has been under a flood warning since Monday. The stadium is enclosed and no plans have been announced to move or cancel the match. A tropical storm watch is already in effect from Sargent, Texas, to Morgan City, Louisiana.
